question.text: `Jeevan Jyoti Foundation`, a public charitable trust in Maharashtra running rural ICU services, is primarily governed by which of the following?

answer.text: Indian Trusts Act 1882 — because all trusts in India fall under this Act
Societies Registration Act 1860 — because charitable trusts must register as societies
Companies Act 2013 Section 8 — because charitable purpose mandates the Section 8 route
Bombay Public Trusts Act 1950 — because it is a public charitable trust operating in Maharashtra

explanation.text: The Logic: Indian Trusts Act 1882 governs PRIVATE trusts. PUBLIC charitable trusts in Maharashtra and Gujarat are governed by the Bombay Public Trusts Act 1950 (renamed Maharashtra Public Trusts Act in 2012), which requires registration with the Charity Commissioner. The Trap: Option A over-extends the 1882 Act — it does not cover public trusts. Option C confuses the society form with trust form — they are distinct vehicles. Option D is optional, not mandatory — a trust need not convert to Section 8. Cross-Exam Context: XXIII tests the private-vs-public trust distinction which rarely surfaces in other NISM exams. Cross-refer to XXIV / IFSCA-01 for AML onboarding of a Maharashtra trust — AML requires the 1950 Act registration number. Assessor's Pro-Tip: During fieldwork of a Maharashtra or Gujarat trust, insist on seeing the 'Schedule-I' registration under the 1950 Act and the Charity Commissioner stamp. Absence of this stamp makes the trust a de-facto private trust — materially changes your legal-compliance disclosure.
